title.en: Abraham Lincoln during the Civil War era
title.zh: 内战时期的亚伯拉罕·林肯

alt.en: Black-and-white head-and-shoulders portrait of Lincoln facing right, with a reproduced signature below.
alt.zh: 林肯面向右侧的黑白半身肖像，下方附有签名复制图。

caption.en: Photographic portrait of Abraham Lincoln, ca. 1860–1865, preserved in the Mathew Brady photographic collection at the National Archives.
caption.zh: 约1860—1865年拍摄的亚伯拉罕·林肯肖像，现存于美国国家档案馆的马修·布雷迪摄影收藏。

interpretation.en: This Civil War-era portrait pairs Lincoln’s face with a reproduced signature. Alongside the Emancipation Proclamation, it connects the president’s public identity with the contested process of emancipation, which also involved enslaved people, abolitionists, Congress and the army.
interpretation.zh: 这幅内战时期的肖像将林肯的面貌与复制签名并置。与《解放宣言》对读，可以把总统的公众形象放进充满争议的解放进程中；被奴役者、废奴主义者、国会与军队也参与其中。

title.en: Ho Chi Minh’s appeal to Truman, first page
title.zh: 胡志明致杜鲁门信函的第一页

alt.en: Typed English letter headed Democratic Republic of Vietnam, Hanoi, January 18, 1946, with handwritten routing notes.
alt.zh: 英文打字信函，抬头为越南民主共和国，注明河内、1946年1月18日，并有手写传阅批注。

caption.en: First page of a three-page letter from Ho Chi Minh to President Harry Truman, 18 January 1946, preserved in U.S. Foreign Service records.
caption.zh: 胡志明于1946年1月18日致美国总统哈里·杜鲁门的三页信函之第一页，存于美国外交机构档案。

interpretation.en: Ho opens with the first United Nations assembly, then invokes Allied wartime cooperation to argue for Vietnamese independence. The letter presents his diplomatic case against renewed French rule through the language of peace and international security.
interpretation.zh: 胡志明先提到联合国第一次大会，再援引战时盟国合作，为越南独立辩护。这封信以和平与国际安全的语言，提出反对法国恢复统治的外交主张。

title.en: Liliʻuokalani’s memorial over Hawaiian Crown lands
title.zh: 莉莉乌奥卡拉尼关于夏威夷王室土地的请愿书

alt.en: Typed petition with handwritten corrections and Liliʻuokalani’s signature at the bottom.
alt.zh: 打字请愿书，附有手写更正，底部为莉莉乌奥卡拉尼的签名。

caption.en: Liliʻuokalani’s signed memorial to the U.S. House of Representatives, 19 December 1898, protested the taking of Hawaiian Crown lands.
caption.zh: 莉莉乌奥卡拉尼于1898年12月19日向美国众议院提交并签署请愿书，抗议夏威夷王室土地被夺取。

interpretation.en: Handwritten additions and the queen’s signature complete this typed appeal to Congress. After the overthrow of the Hawaiian monarchy and U.S. annexation, Liliʻuokalani continued to press claims to Crown lands through petitions and legal argument.
interpretation.zh: 手写增补与女王签名完善了这份提交国会的打字申诉。夏威夷君主制遭推翻、美国吞并夏威夷后，莉莉乌奥卡拉尼仍通过请愿与法律论证争取王室土地权利。

title.en: Ida B. Wells appeals for the Baker family
title.zh: 艾达·B·威尔斯为贝克家属求助

alt.en: Handwritten first page addressed to Mr. Dawes, describing injuries, medical neglect and the Baker family’s lack of food and shelter.
alt.zh: 致道斯先生的手写信第一页，叙述贝克家属的伤情、医疗延误及缺乏食物和住处的困境。

caption.en: First page of Ida B. Wells’s 1898 letter to Mr. Dawes seeking federal help for the family of Frazier Baker, murdered with his young daughter in South Carolina.
caption.zh: 艾达·B·威尔斯1898年致道斯先生信函的第一页，为在南卡罗来纳州与幼女一同遇害的弗雷泽·贝克的家属争取联邦援助。

interpretation.en: Wells combined investigation and public campaigning with practical advocacy for survivors of racist violence. Here her appeal for congressional relief connects anti-lynching work to the immediate needs of an injured, impoverished family.
interpretation.zh: 威尔斯将调查、公共宣传与为种族暴力幸存者争取实际援助结合起来。她在信中呼吁国会救济，把反私刑运动与一个受伤且陷入贫困家庭的迫切需要联系起来。

title.en: Dolores Huerta at the Chávez monument dedication
title.zh: 多洛雷斯·韦尔塔参加查韦斯纪念地揭幕活动

alt.en: Barack Obama and four visitors in César Chávez’s preserved office; Dolores Huerta stands in a red jacket immediately to the viewer’s right of Obama.
alt.zh: 奥巴马与四位访客在塞萨尔·查韦斯保存下来的办公室内；穿红色外套的多洛雷斯·韦尔塔站在画面中奥巴马右侧。

caption.en: Dolores Huerta joins Barack Obama, Arturo Rodriguez, Helen Chávez and Paul Chávez in César Chávez’s office in Keene, California, 8 October 2012, before the national monument dedication. Official White House photograph by Pete Souza.
caption.zh: 2012年10月8日，国家纪念地揭幕前，多洛雷斯·韦尔塔与奥巴马、阿图罗·罗德里格斯、海伦·查韦斯及保罗·查韦斯来到加州基恩的塞萨尔·查韦斯办公室。白宫官方摄影师皮特·苏扎摄。

interpretation.en: Books, a painted portrait and the preserved office frame a later recognition of farmworker organizing. Huerta’s 2012 visit with Obama belongs to the movement’s public commemoration, decades after the strikes and bargaining campaigns.
interpretation.zh: 书籍、绘画肖像与保存下来的办公室，构成社会纪念农场工人组织运动的场景。韦尔塔在2012年与奥巴马到访此地，距离当年的罢工与谈判已有数十年。

title.en: German unity in a U.S. presidential proclamation
title.zh: 美国总统公告中的德国统一

alt.en: First page of Presidential Proclamation 6194, headed German-American Day, 1990, describing a reunited Germany.
alt.zh: 第6194号总统公告第一页，标题为“1990年德裔美国人日”，正文提及重新统一的德国。

caption.en: First page of U.S. Presidential Proclamation 6194, issued by George H. W. Bush on 3 October 1990, marking German-American Day as Germany reunited.
caption.zh: 美国总统乔治·H·W·布什于1990年10月3日发布的第6194号公告之第一页，在德国统一之际纪念德裔美国人日。

interpretation.en: The proclamation links German immigration to America with reunification in 1990. Its account presents unity from the perspective of a U.S. ally on the day East and West Germany united, connecting a major diplomatic change with an annual commemoration.
interpretation.zh: 公告将德国人移民美国的历史与1990年的统一相联系。在东西德合一的当天，它从美国盟友的立场描述统一，将重大的外交变化与一年一度的纪念日结合。

title.en: Rosa Parks’s seat in a court exhibit
title.zh: 法庭证物中的罗莎·帕克斯座位

alt.en: A bus seating diagram with circles for passengers and an arrow labeled Rosa Parks; exhibit annotations appear at upper left.
alt.zh: 公交车座位示意图以圆圈表示乘客，箭头标注罗莎·帕克斯的位置；左上角有证物批注。

caption.en: Bus seating diagram used in Browder v. Gayle, the federal case challenging Montgomery bus segregation. NARA catalogs the document to 5 June 1956; an exhibit annotation on the sheet is dated 22 February 1956.
caption.zh: 布劳德诉盖尔案中使用的公交车座位示意图；该联邦案件挑战蒙哥马利的公交隔离制度。美国国家档案馆将文件日期编为1956年6月5日，纸面证物批注另载1956年2月22日。

interpretation.en: Rows of outlined seats and the handwritten label identify the place attributed to Parks’s refusal on 1 December 1955. A segregated everyday space became courtroom evidence. The boycott’s collective organizing and the separate federal lawsuit challenged the same system through different means.
interpretation.zh: 一排排座位轮廓与手写标注，指出帕克斯在1955年12月1日拒绝让座时被认定的位置。日常的隔离空间成为法庭证据。抵制运动的集体组织与另行提起的联邦诉讼，以不同方式挑战同一制度。
